chose: dedupe on a stored `metric` label, one OPEN conjecture per label at a time — and a RESOLVED one keeps the label quiet until the value moves a further threshold-width past the value that was resolved
over: dedupe on the content-hash id (the existing mechanism) — it cannot work, because the value is IN the observation text and changes every run, so ten runs mint ten ids and ten open questions

dedupe on label forever, so a label that ever produced a conjecture never produces another — that trades the spam generator for a silence generator: the second, larger excursion is exactly the one worth asking about
dedupe on a time window (one conjecture per label per day/run) — a clock is not the identity of a question, and it re-opens on a schedule rather than on new evidence
because: the identity of the QUESTION is 'why is <label> outside its band', which is stable across runs while the number is not. So the dedupe key must be the label, not the measurement. The resolved-state rule falls out of the same reading: a resolution answers the excursion it was written against, so an excursion that has moved a further threshold-width beyond the resolved value is a DIFFERENT question and deserves to be asked. Requires storing `value` on the record, which the journal wanted anyway

chose: return-to-band NEVER auto-resolves; it prints the open conjecture's id and the exact `coherence resolved` line instead
over: auto-resolve when the metric comes back inside its band
auto-retract the conjecture on return, on the theory that the observation stopped holding
because: a resolution's `because` field is what the discriminating test SHOWED. A number wandering back shows nothing about the cause, so an auto-resolution would have to write a false claim ('it came back') into the one field that carries evidence. The failure is also silent and asymmetric: it deletes an entry from `decisions --open` — the single list this feature exists to populate — and deletes it precisely in the case where nobody looked. And it closes the most interesting questions preferentially: a metric that left its band and returned has usually done something stranger (a transient, an accidental revert, a non-monotonicity) than one that stayed out. Silence is the other failure, so the return IS reported — on stdout, as evidence a human may resolve WITH, never as the resolution

chose: an explained move (--why) is written as a conjecture PLUS its resolution — born answered — and when a conjecture is already open for that label the --why RESOLVES it
over: a plain `decision` record: it would land in Standing with an empty `over`, reporting a metric move as a settled choice
a new record kind `observation`, with its own render section
writing nothing at all when --why is present, on the grounds that the source file already holds the explanation
because: the journal already has exactly the shape 'a notable move, and what accounted for it': a conjecture with a resolution pointing at it. Reusing it means an explained-immediately move and an explained-three-weeks-later move render identically, which is correct — the reader cares what the answer is, not how fast it arrived. It also needs no new kind, no new render branch, and no change to resolve(). The open-conjecture case is the loop closing itself: coherence asked the question, the project filled in the `why` field its own table already has, and the next harness run carries that answer back in

chose: match the consuming table's `Math.abs(delta) >= threshold` byte-for-byte, float wobble included, instead of adding an epsilon or a relative tolerance
over: an epsilon around the threshold, so a move of 'exactly one band' in decimal counts as notable
a relative comparison (|delta| / |baseline|) so the bar scales with the metric
because: measured while writing the test: 0.15 - 0.14 is 0.00999999999999998, so a decimal move that LOOKS like exactly one band is under a 0.010 threshold and the row prints as not-moved. Any correction here would be a correction coherence applied and planetizer did not, and the two halves would then disagree exactly at the boundary — the one place a disagreement is invisible, because it is the case nobody eyeballs. Being wrong the SAME way is worth more than being right alone. The relative form is worse still: notableDelta is an ABSOLUTE physical quantity (o2's 0.01 is a tenth of the O2_ANIMAL_MIN..O2_FIRE_THRESHOLD band), and dividing it by the baseline would silently re-scale a bar the project derived from the manual. Pinned in test/observed.test.ts as a fact, not routed around

chose: negative controls on BOTH new behaviours: the label dedupe and the refusal to auto-resolve
over: one negative control on the dedupe only, since it is the load-bearing one
because: ran two. (1) DEDUPE: replaced the lookup key with the observation TEXT instead of the label — the exact failure the design exists to avoid, identity of the measurement rather than identity of the question. 9 of 23 went red; the load-bearing one said 'runs 2..10 ask nothing new: false !== true' and the journal held ten open conjectures for one question. (2) RETURN-TO-BAND: made a return inside the band resolve the open conjecture with because='the metric returned to its band'. Exactly 3 red, and the message is the argument itself: actual 'resolved', expected 'returned-to-band', plus 'one question, still unanswered: 0 !== 1'. Restored byte-identical against a saved copy both times (diff clean), 356/356 after. Two controls rather than one because the return-to-band rule is a JUDGEMENT rather than a mechanism — it is the behaviour a later pass is most likely to 'fix' into auto-resolution, so it is the one that most needs a test somebody has watched fail

chose: usage errors exit 2, against the brief's letter of 'exit code 0 always'
over: exit 0 unconditionally, including on --value banana or a missing --threshold, as literally specified
because: the brief's 'exit 0 always. This gates nothing' is about the OBSERVATION — a metric outside its band must never fail a build, and it does not: outside, inside, opened, deduped, resolved all exit 0, pinned by a CLI test. A malformed invocation is not an observation. Exiting 0 on a typo'd flag would make the harness stop asking questions silently, which is this repo's own named defect ('a command that exits 0 and does nothing, which is the defect this harness exists to hunt', cli.ts resolved branch) and the same failure as the negative control whose regex never matched. --threshold in particular has no default and must not acquire one: the bar is domain knowledge that lives on the project's side of the seam, so a missing one is a missing BAR, not a zero

chose: leave `observed` out of agentInstructions — the text every agent is handed at startup
over: adding a fourth verb to the startup instruction alongside decide/blocked/conjecture/retract
because: that string is paid for by every agent on every job, and the conjecture pass already logged an open question about whether agents reach for a verb they were not told about (d-04198572). But observed is not an agent verb: its caller is a harness with a metric table, once per row per run. An agent that needs it is an agent BUILDING the harness, and that agent is reading the README, where the division of labour now lives. Adding it would spend the one budget the journal cannot overdraw to teach a verb its audience never invokes
